researchFocus: Search as archival discovery for eighteenth-century intellectual history
about: I am a doctoral researcher at the University of Helsinki, working on language models for eighteenth-century intellectual history. I am interested in search as a form of archival discovery: how computational systems can make meaningful passages visible, retrieve implicit connections across large archives, and still remain accountable to historical interpretation.

This work sits between digital humanities and NLP. It uses large digitized archives such as ECCO, dense text representations, expert annotation, and close reading to ask when model similarity becomes usable historical evidence. Before Helsinki, I completed a master's degree in computer science at ShanghaiTech University, where I worked on vision-language reasoning and multimodal machine learning.

researchDirections.title: Digital humanities and historical archives
researchDirections.description: Using language models and semantic search to support intellectual history, reception studies, and discovery in large-scale historical collections.

researchDirections.title: AI diagnosis and evaluation
researchDirections.description: Diagnosing what models capture, miss, or distort in difficult data: noisy OCR, mixed languages, implicit meaning, and historically distant contexts.

researchDirections.title: Matching and reasoning algorithms
researchDirections.description: Developing semantic matching, relation reasoning, and multimodal representation methods, extending my earlier work on vision-language reasoning.

currentWork.label: Current Work
currentWork.title: Archival search for intellectual history
currentWork.description: My current work combines textual unit identification, semantic representation evaluation, calibrated search, and close reading. It is part of CASCADE, an EU MSCA Doctoral Network on Computational Analysis of Semantic Change Across Different Environments.
